entries.title: Script imports resolve from project root, not importing file
entries.missing: import { state } from "./game_state.js" inside scripts/player.js fails (Cannot load module 'game_state.js'); relative specifiers are resolved against the project root, which contradicts normal ES module semantics and is not documented in scripting doc.
entries.workaround: Used project-root paths: import ... from "scripts/game_state.js"
entries.suggestion: Resolve ./ and ../ relative to the importing module (or document the root-relative rule in docs/SCRIPTING.md and mention it in the validate hint).
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: './x.js' and '../x.js' now resolve relative to the importing module ('scripts/x.js' stays project-root relative); escaping the project root is an error naming the import. Documented in docs/SCRIPTING.md > Imports.

entries.title: Unknown Script.props only warned at runtime, not by validate
entries.missing: Script props not declared as class fields (props.sceneName on Level) are only reported as a WARN during run; factoria validate says OK.
entries.workaround: Removed the prop manually after seeing the run log.
entries.suggestion: Have validate instantiate/inspect script class fields and flag unknown props with did-you-mean.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: factoria validate now reports Script.props that are not class fields (warning with did-you-mean). Declare props as class fields.

entries.title: Generated types/factoria.d.ts is a placeholder (any)
entries.missing: factoria new writes a placeholder d.ts where every import is 'any', so @ts-check gives no help; real typings only via 'factoria api --dts' which AGENTS.md says to regenerate but new does not run.
entries.workaround: Relied on docs; did not use typings.
entries.suggestion: factoria new should write the real generated typings.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: factoria new writes the real generated typings to types/factoria.d.ts; refresh with 'factoria api --dts --project .'. Remove the placeholder workaround.

entries.title: Template docs contradict: AGENTS.md says 2D origin is screen centre, camera needs manual placement for tilemap levels
entries.missing: No documented recipe for a level-bounds-clamped follow camera (both axes) nor for how Camera view size relates to orthoSize/design size when the window is resized; had to write follow_camera clamp by hand.
entries.workaround: scripts/follow_camera.js with minX/maxX/minY/maxY props and hardcoded 1280x720 view.
entries.suggestion: Add CameraFollow2D component or camera.viewSize / game.screenSize-based bounds clamp helper; document.
notes: Still open after e2b0090: no CameraFollow2D / level-bounds clamp helper; docs/AI_GUIDE.md 9.6 only shows an unclamped follow camera.
Docs: AI_GUIDE 9.6 'Camera follow with level bounds' recipe; AGENTS.md conventions on 2D origin.
Since ad0922f: entity.bounds() gives a Tilemap's world rectangle; follow_camera.js clamps to it ("bounds": "map") and no scene carries hand-set camera limits.

entries.title: rng cannot be seeded from script or tool arguments
entries.missing: project.generate_level takes a seed parameter, but RngAPI has only float/range/int/chance/pick/shuffle; no rng.seed(n) or rng.fork(seed), so seed->level determinism is impossible with the engine rng.
entries.workaround: Implemented mulberry32 PRNG inside the tool.
entries.suggestion: Add rng.seed(n) and/or rng.create(seed) returning an independent generator.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: rng.seed(n) reseeds the world RNG (seed -> level determinism in tools and tests).
Since ad0922f: rng.create(seed) is an independent seeded generator that never touches the world RNG; tools/generate_level.js uses it instead of its own PRNG.

entries.title: raycast starting inside a collider returns the owner at distance 0
entries.missing: physics.raycast from an entity's centre returned its own entity at distance 0 (normal [0,0]), so a patrol enemy turned around every tick and never moved; no option to ignore an entity or exclude self, and docs do not mention it.
entries.workaround: Start rays outside the own collider (offset by half width + 2 px).
entries.suggestion: Add raycast option {ignore: entity|id} (or auto-ignore the origin's own collider), document inside-start behaviour.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: physics.raycast(a, b, { ignore: this.entity }) / raycast3d(..., { ignore }); colliders containing the ray origin are skipped; triggers skipped unless ignoreTriggers:false.

entries.title: No built-in patrol/ledge sensing or ground/wall query helpers
entries.missing: Enemy AI needs wall and ledge detection; only raycast exists (returns full entity JSON incl. huge Tilemap tiles array when stringified), no shape-cast, no contact-normal query for current contacts, no isTouchingWall.
entries.workaround: Two raycasts per fixed step in scripts/enemy.js.
entries.suggestion: Add entity.isTouching(dir) / physics.shapeCast and a lighter raycast result (entity id).
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Use entity.isTouching([1,0]) (wall right) / isTouching([0,1]) (ceiling) / isGrounded(), and a short downward physics.raycast with { ignore } for ledge checks. No shape-cast yet (see ROADMAP).

entries.title: ParticleEmitter burst is silently suppressed when emitting=false; no one-shot auto-destroy
entries.missing: Docs say burst fires 'once when the emitter starts', but emitting:false (the natural choice for one-shot) emits nothing. Also no autoDestroy/oneShot flag, so every coin pickup needs a timer to destroy the emitter entity.
entries.workaround: Use emitting:true with rate:0 and burst:N, and this.after(1, destroy).
entries.suggestion: Add ParticleEmitter oneShot/destroyOnFinish and document that burst needs emitting=true (or make burst independent).
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: ParticleEmitter.burst fires with emitting:false; particles.burst(entity, n) / entity.emitBurst(n) spawn on demand; ParticleEmitter.autoDestroy:true destroys the entity when the burst finishes. Drop the cleanup timers.

entries.title: fs.write / fs.* commands unavailable to scripts inside factoria test
entries.missing: A project tool that calls fa.call('fs.write') works via 'factoria call' but throws Unknown command 'fs.write' when the same tool runs inside a test (headless test engine's registry lacks fs.*). docs/extending shows fs.write for level generators.
entries.workaround: Added a dryRun argument returning the scene JSON; test checks the JSON and loads a committed generated file instead.
entries.suggestion: Register fs.* in the test runtime (sandboxed to project), or provide game.writeFile / a way for tests to load a scene from JSON (game.loadJson).
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Use game.loadJson(sceneObject) in tests to load a scene from data (no fs.* needed). fs.* is still not registered in the test runtime.

entries.title: No documented cross-scene persistent state
entries.missing: Lives/coins must survive scene.load (which drops all entities and listeners). Docs mention only storage (persistent save data on disk) and nothing about per-session global state.
entries.workaround: Module-level singleton scripts/game_state.js exported object (it persists between scenes and is shared with tests).
entries.suggestion: Document module-singleton persistence guarantee or add game.session / world.persistent state; make hot reload semantics clear.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Import { session } from 'factoria': a plain object that survives scene loads for the run (reset per test file). Module-level variables also persist across scene loads.

entries.title: Tests cannot reset state between tests except by reloading scenes; module state leaks
entries.missing: Module-level state (above) is not reset between tests; had to call resetState() manually in each test. No beforeEach at top level documented (only inside describe).
entries.workaround: load() helper calls resetState().
entries.suggestion: Reload project modules between test files/tests or document the isolation rules; allow top-level beforeEach.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Each test FILE now gets fresh module instances, empty in-memory storage and empty session. Within one file state still carries over (reset it yourself); top-level beforeEach is still only inside describe.

entries.title: factoria call runs each command in a fresh process, so game.step then script.eval do not share state
entries.missing: CLI 'factoria call game.step' followed by 'factoria call script.eval' shows an unstepped world; only MCP keeps a session. docs/cli does not say so clearly; debugging required writing a Python MCP stdio client.
entries.workaround: Small Python JSON-RPC client over 'factoria mcp'.
entries.suggestion: Add 'factoria repl' / 'factoria call --steps N' / a --session flag, and state in call --help that it is stateless.
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Use 'factoria session' (JSON lines on one engine) or 'factoria call --batch [...]' (commands in order on one engine); 'factoria call' also takes --frames-before/--press/--input. call --help states that a single call is stateless.

entries.title: No one-way platforms
entries.missing: Collider2D has no oneWay option; all brick platforms are fully solid, so the player cannot jump up through them from below (ai-guide 9.5 also notes this).
entries.workaround: Dropped: platforms are solid; levels designed so headroom is clear.
entries.suggestion: Add Collider2D oneWay field enforced by physics, also for Tilemap solid tiles (per-tile one-way list).
notes: Fixed in e2b0090: Collider2D.oneWay:true (verified: body jumps up through the platform and lands on it).

entries.title: Tilemap has no per-tile entity hooks (coins/enemies/spawn must be separate entities)
entries.missing: Levels need object placement from a map; Tilemap only holds tile indices, no object layer, and no editor/ASCII import, so I wrote an external Python ASCII->scene builder and a JS generator.
entries.workaround: Scene generation scripts (scratch + tools/generate_level.js).
entries.suggestion: Tilemap object layer or 'scene.import_ascii' / 'tilemap.paint' commands; tile-to-prefab mapping.
notes: Still open after e2b0090: no tilemap object layer or ASCII/prefab import command.

Fixed in ae8bb15: scene.import_ascii {rows, legend, tilemap, position, anchor, save} builds the Tilemap and spawns prefabs (coins, enemies, a player spawn with a fixed id) at the cell centres, tagged tilemap:<entity>; re-importing replaces them. tools/generate_level.js can be replaced by one call with the level's ASCII rows (AI_GUIDE 9.8).

Workaround removed in 9dc7fd5: levels/level1.json and level2.json are ASCII maps built with scene.import_ascii (file mode with "path" since cc789f7); generate_level composes rows and builds through the same command.

entries.title: No way to verify audio events in tests
entries.missing: game.* test API cannot assert that audio.play was called (jump/coin/stomp/hurt sounds are untestable); only --record-audio on run.
entries.workaround: Checked --record-audio output non-empty; no assertion in tests.
entries.suggestion: Add game.audioLog() / expect(audio).toHavePlayed(path) in tests.
notes: Still open after e2b0090: no audio log / assertion in the test harness.

Fixed in ebb054d: game.audioLog() lists every sound played since the test started ({frame, path, volume, bus, source, ok}); assert with expect(game.audioLog()).toContainPlayed("jump.wav", { times: 1 }) (alias toHavePlayed). MCP/CLI agents use the audio.log command. tests/platformer.test.js now asserts the jump, coin, stomp, hurt and win sounds.

entries.title: Tilemap collision details undocumented (ghost edges, solid tile index semantics, trigger vs tile)
entries.missing: Docs do not state whether tilemap colliders are merged into larger shapes (affects ghost-collision with friction 0 players), nor the physics layer/mask of tile colliders.
entries.workaround: Used friction 0 on characters; no issues seen in tests.
entries.suggestion: Document how Tilemap collision is generated.
notes: Still open after e2b0090: tilemap collision rules are written in engine/physics/include/fa/physics/physics.h (merged row boxes, friction 0.5, not one-way, no trigger events) but not in docs/*.md.
Docs: AI_GUIDE 9.8 documents tilemap collision (merging, solidTiles, origin, one-way via separate oneWay entity).

entries.title: Commands only edit the running world
entries.missing: scene.import_ascii, scene.load and scene.save act on the running world (scene.load stops audio and resets physics), so a generator must load a base scene, import, save and reload the previous scene, losing unsaved runtime state.
entries.workaround: generate_level loaded the base scene, imported, saved and restored the running scene (9dc7fd5).
entries.suggestion: A file-targeted mode for scene.import_ascii, or scene.load_json / scene.export.
notes: Fixed in cc789f7: scene.import_ascii {path, from, dryRun} edits a scene FILE in a scratch world and never touches the running game; generate_level uses it.

entries.title: fs.delete refuses .factoria/ while scene.save can write there
entries.missing: A tool could write scratch scenes into .factoria/ with scene.save but could not delete them with fs.delete.
entries.workaround: Avoided scratch files in dryRun.
entries.suggestion: One consistent rule for writing and deleting, with a scratch folder.
notes: Fixed in cc789f7: .factoria/tmp/ is a scratch folder where scene.save, scene.import_ascii path, fs.write, fs.edit and fs.delete may all write and delete; the rest of .factoria/ is managed by the engine.

entries.title: Bug: factoria run --input resolves against the current directory
entries.missing: factoria run <project> --input replays/run.json from another folder failed, and the hint wrongly said the path is relative to the project root.
entries.workaround: Ran the replay from the project folder.
entries.suggestion: Resolve input files against the project too and make the hint list the locations tried.
notes: Fixed in cc789f7: input paths (--input, @args, --batch-file) try the current directory, then the project; a missing file lists every location tried. Outputs are relative to the current directory and reported as absolute paths.

entries.title: scene.import_ascii with save overwrites the main scene without --scene
entries.missing: factoria call scene.import_ascii @map.json with save:true and no --scene loads the main scene and overwrites it with the wrong map.
entries.workaround: Documented that --scene must always be passed.
entries.suggestion: A path argument on scene.import_ascii, or refuse that save.
notes: Fixed in cc789f7: the map files carry "path"; save without path is refused (unsafe_save) when the running scene is only the implicit mainScene.

entries.title: No file-targeted component edits
entries.missing: To set the camera height, sky colour and level number of a generated level, generate_level writes a patched copy of the base scene with fs.write; there is no scene-file equivalent of scene.set_component.
entries.workaround: tools/generate_level.js writes .factoria/tmp/generate_level.base.scene.json and passes it as 'from'.
entries.suggestion: An 'edits' argument on scene.import_ascii, or scene.set_component with a path.
notes: Fixed in 6e5b5b2: scene.import_ascii takes edits {"<entity id>": {"<Component>": {fields}}} in file mode, applied like scene.set_component before the file is written. Workaround removed: tools/generate_level.js passes from + edits and no longer writes a scratch base copy.

entries.title: Scene files are not written atomically
entries.missing: fs::write_bytes truncates then writes, so a crash mid-write can leave a half-written scene.
entries.workaround: None.
entries.suggestion: Write to a temporary file and rename it over the target.
notes: Fixed in 6e5b5b2: fs::write_bytes (and the tooling writer behind fs.write, scaffold and export) writes a temporary file next to the target and renames it over it; on any failure the original is left untouched.

entries.title: No script query for a texture's size
entries.missing: Scripts cannot ask a Sprite's texture size; entity.bounds() decodes the image file itself to know it.
entries.workaround: None in the game.
entries.suggestion: A renderer-side texture size query exposed to scripts.
notes: Fixed in 303db3e: assets.textureSize(path) returns { width, height }, the same cached size entity.bounds() uses (32 x 32 for a missing file).
